subject: Geography
description: Forest types, biomes, Forest Survey data, mangroves

questions.stem: India's forest cover is approximately what % of its total geographical area (as per recent ISFR)?
questions.explanation: Forest cover ~21-22% of geographical area (ISFR reports by FSI, Dehradun). National Forest Policy (1988) target: 33% (66% in hills). Madhya Pradesh has the largest forest area in km²; Mizoram has the highest forest cover as % of state area.
questions.subject: Geography

options.option_text: Bhitarkanika (Odisha)
Sundarbans (West Bengal)
Pichavaram (Tamil Nadu)
Coringa (Andhra Pradesh)

questions.explanation: Sundarbans — largest mangrove forest in India and the world (with Bangladesh portion). ~2,120 sq km in India. Home to Royal Bengal Tigers, estuarine crocodiles. UNESCO WHS. Bhitarkanika is second; Pichavaram is a scenic third.

questions.stem: The TROPICAL RAIN FORESTS in India are found mainly in:

options.option_text: Rajasthan
Western Ghats + Andamans + North-East India
Punjab plains
Deccan plateau

questions.explanation: Tropical rainforests — very high rainfall (>200 cm) areas. In India: windward (western) slopes of Western Ghats (Kerala, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu), parts of Andaman & Nicobar, and NE states. Evergreen, dense, multi-storied. Rosewood, mahogany, ebony.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Match the FOREST TYPE with the TREE. A. Tropical evergreen.  B. Tropical deciduous.  C. Desert.  D. Mangrove. List-II: 1. Rosewood, mahogany.  2. Teak, sal.  3. Babool (Acacia), khejri.  4. Sundari, keora.
questions.explanation: Evergreen — rosewood, mahogany (Western Ghats). Deciduous (monsoon) — teak, sal, bamboo (MP, Jharkhand, Maharashtra). Desert/thorn — babool, khejri, kikar (Rajasthan, Punjab). Mangrove — sundari, keora, mangium (deltas, Sundarbans — named after 'sundari' tree).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The state with the HIGHEST PERCENTAGE of forest cover (as % of state area) is:

options.option_text: Madhya Pradesh
Mizoram
Uttar Pradesh
Rajasthan

questions.explanation: Mizoram — ~85% of geographical area is forested (highest in India). Madhya Pradesh has the LARGEST forest area in absolute km². Punjab/Haryana have very low forest cover (~3-5%). ISFR tracks these annually. ~85% of its area.

questions.stem: 'SILENT VALLEY' — a famous biodiversity-rich evergreen forest — is in which state?

options.option_text: Karnataka
Kerala
Tamil Nadu
Andhra Pradesh

questions.explanation: Silent Valley National Park — Palakkad district, Kerala. Famous for lion-tailed macaque. 1973 hydroelectric project was dropped after environmental campaign (early major environmental victory). Declared NP in 1984.
questions.subject: Geography

options.option_text: Evergreen trees
Deciduous trees
Mangrove species
Desert plants

questions.explanation: Teak (Tectona grandis) and Sal (Shorea robusta) — both DECIDUOUS trees, shedding leaves in the dry season. Teak prized for furniture (termite-resistant). Sal common in UP, MP, Odisha, Jharkhand forests. shed leaves seasonally.

questions.stem: Van Mahotsav — India's annual week-long tree-planting festival observed every July — was launched in 1950 by which Union Cabinet Minister?

options.option_text: Jawaharlal Nehru, the first Prime Minister of India
K.M. Munshi, then Union Minister of Food and Agriculture
Rajendra Prasad, the first President of the Republic
Sardar Patel, then Union Home Minister of independent India

questions.explanation: K.M. Munshi (Kanaiyalal Maneklal Munshi) initiated Van Mahotsav in 1950 while serving as Union Minister of Food and Agriculture, intending to create mass awareness about afforestation. Nehru and Rajendra Prasad are frequently confused as the founders because of their visibility, but the initiative was Munshi's specific policy drive.

questions.stem: 'Shola' forests — patches of dense subtropical montane forest nestled within rolling grasslands — are primarily concentrated in which mountain system of India?

options.option_text: Eastern Ghats ranges of Andhra Pradesh and Odisha state
Nilgiri and Anaimalai massifs of the southern Western Ghats
Vindhya and Satpura ranges of central peninsular India
Shivalik foothills running along the Himalayan sub-zone

questions.explanation: Shola forests are characteristic of high-altitude (above ~1,500 m) valleys in the Nilgiris, Anaimalais, and Palani hills of the Western Ghats. They form a mosaic with montane grasslands (vayals). The Eastern Ghats are too dry and low-altitude, while the Vindhyas and Shivaliks have entirely different vegetation regimes.

questions.stem: The Indian Forest Act of 1927 legally recognises three categories of forests. Which of the following is NOT one of them?

options.option_text: Reserved Forests — under the strictest government control
Protected Forests — with partial user-rights restrictions
Community Forests — managed by elected local panchayats
Village Forests — assigned to local village communities

questions.explanation: The Indian Forest Act, 1927 defines only three categories: Reserved Forests (Sections 3–27), Protected Forests (Sections 29–34), and Village Forests (Section 28). 'Community Forests' is not a statutory category under this Act; it is often confused with Village Forests or with community forest rights under the Forest Rights Act, 2006.

questions.stem: Tropical moist deciduous forests — which cover the largest area of any single forest type in India — are associated with which mean annual rainfall range?

options.option_text: 50 to 100 cm, supporting drought-adapted open woodlands
100 to 200 cm, enabling seasonal canopy and dense undergrowth
200 to 250 cm, producing near-perennial canopy conditions
25 to 50 cm, overlapping with thorny scrub vegetation zones

questions.explanation: Tropical moist deciduous forests receive 100–200 cm of rainfall annually. Below 100 cm, dry deciduous forests dominate; above 200 cm, conditions favour semi-evergreen or wet evergreen species. The 200–250 cm range is tempting but applies to tropical semi-evergreen or moist evergreen forests, not moist deciduous.

questions.stem: Which of the following pairs CORRECTLY matches a tree species with the forest type where it is a dominant ecological indicator?

options.option_text: Chir Pine — tropical moist deciduous forests of the Deccan
Sundari — tidal and mangrove forests of the Bengal delta coast
Sandalwood — alpine and subalpine forests of the Jammu region
Tendu (Ebony) — montane temperate forests of the Western Ghats

questions.explanation: The Sundari tree (Heritiera fomes) is so dominant in the Bengal delta mangroves that it gives the Sundarbans its name. Chir Pine (Pinus roxburghii) is a Himalayan subtropical pine species, not a Deccan deciduous tree. Sandalwood grows in tropical dry deciduous forests of Karnataka, not alpine zones. Tendu (Diospyros melanoxylon) is a dry deciduous species, not a Western Ghats montane tree.

questions.stem: The Forest Survey of India (FSI) maps 'forest cover' via satellite imagery using specific thresholds. What minimum canopy density AND minimum patch area must a land parcel meet to be counted as forest cover in India?

options.option_text: 25% canopy density threshold over a minimum of 0.5 hectares
10% canopy density threshold over a minimum of 1.0 hectare
10% canopy density threshold over a minimum of 0.5 hectares
25% canopy density threshold over a minimum of 1.0 hectare

questions.explanation: FSI applies the globally aligned threshold of ≥10% canopy cover (crown density) over a minimum contiguous area of 1.0 hectare for a patch to qualify as forest cover. The 0.5-hectare figure applies to FAO's FRA methodology for some countries but NOT to India's ISFR. Candidates often confuse the area threshold (1 ha) or inflate the density to 25%, leading to all four options appearing plausible.

questions.stem: The 'gurjan' timber-yielding trees belonging to the genus Dipterocarpus — which also give valuable resin used in varnishes — form extensive forests in which specific region of India?

options.option_text: Cold temperate oak-rhododendron forests of Uttarakhand belt
Tropical moist evergreen forests of the Andaman Islands
Dry deciduous forests of eastern Rajasthan and Gujarat belt
Subtropical pine forests of the Meghalaya plateau interior

questions.explanation: Dipterocarpus trees (gurjan) are hallmark species of the Andaman Islands' tropical moist evergreen forests, and also appear in parts of northeast India (Assam). The Andaman archipelago hosts several Dipterocarpaceae species not found on the Indian mainland. Uttarakhand's temperate belt and Meghalaya's pine forests have entirely different floristic assemblages; Rajasthan's dry zone cannot support these moisture-demanding tall trees.
